thought.text:
All 4 tests pass. Note that in my terminal verification, the shell passed literal backslash-n and backslash-t strings (as `\\n`, `\\t`) because I used single-quoted shell strings with `\n` which isn't interpreted by bash within single quotes — the actual string contained backslash chars, not real tabs/newlines. That's why the CLI showed `north\\tdock`. The real test suite (which uses actual tab `\t` and newline `\n` characters in Python string literals) passes, as verified above.

Let me redo the CLI verification with actual control characters to be thorough, and also verify edge cases (preserving digits and hyphens, multiple whitespace, etc.).

action.command:
cd /workshop/fixture && python3 -B -c "
from routekit.cli import main
import contextlib, io, json
for z in [' North\tDock ', ' East \n Gate ', ' West  Wing ', ' SOUTH-2 ', 'a   b\t c', 'already-here', 'zone 123 4x', '  pad  ']:
    out=io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out): main(['manifest', z])
    print(repr(z), '->', json.loads(out.getvalue()))
from routekit.zones import canonical_zone
from routekit.labels import zone_label
print(canonical_zone(' \t  \n '))  # only whitespace
print(zone_label(' West  Wing '))
"
